own_solution.law: Steady radial conduction in a cylindrical shell: dT = (Tin - Tout) ln(rm/r1)/ln(r2/r1)
assumptions: fixed surface temperatures at r1 and at the outermost insulation surface

notes: All strata match my pass 1. Checked certified R answers: q=1.2 cm: 120*0.51083/ln(3.4)=61.299/1.22378=50.09 K; q=1.8: 61.299/1.28093=47.855 K; q=2.5: 61.299/ln(3.8333)=61.299/1.34373=45.618 K; base 55.797 K. k cancels exactly. Minimal pairs: T6641/T21B1 share '1.8 cm of the same insulation ... round the layer on the pipe' and differ only in the temporal attachment; T8754/T15F5 differ only in pipe layer vs tank. Numeral-free twins T26FA (of T6641) and T6E73 (of T8754) match their twins' wording with the number replaced. The R wiring relies on 'outermost surface of the insulation is held at 300 K' carrying over to the new outer surface; this is the natural reading of 'outermost'.
